entry.title: Aquilegia parviflora (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the small flowers that give Aquilegia parviflora (pictured) its name make it unpopular with gardeners?

entry.title: Gerhard Schwedes (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the first draft pick in New England Patriots' history, Gerhard Schwedes, was born in Nazi Germany?

entry.title: an ancient Egyptian pet cemetery (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that an ancient Egyptian pet cemetery included a Rüppell's fox, a Barbary falcon, and over 500 cats?

entry.title: Theresia Bauer (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Theresia Bauer was named science minister of the year four times?

entry.title: a species of Australian ant (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a species of Australian ant has special workers that make honey, and is considered a delicacy by Aboriginal Australians?

entry.title: Armand Ceritano (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Armand Ceritano acquired a Philadelphia hotel for "a smile and a handshake" – and $20, borrowed from others?

entry.title: Orphic Hymns (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that in the Orphic Hymns the mythical Greek hero Heracles is a sun god?

entry.title: Clay Stevenson (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Clay Stevenson has his nickname, "Mud", written on the front of his mask, and a Star of Life on the back?

entry.title: a Colorado TV station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a volunteer quipped that a Colorado TV station "broadcast to more ears of corn and heads of cattle than any other station"?
